column3: The error must be subpolynomial for every epsilon, not merely o(sqrt(x)); finite Sidon constructions or a better constant cannot settle this. No uniform error mechanism.

Two separate cubic-graph assertions include an iff characterization by trilobites. The induced 2-regular maximum and (1,2)-domination definitions must be reconciled in the primary body before a finite witness search; none performed.

The inequality uses average neighborhood independence and a maximum-leaf spanning tree on every connected graph. Charging neighborhood independent sets to one tree is a possible route, but no simultaneous averaging lemma established; registry/GitHub route forbidden.

Relevant minimum-degree hypothesis is unspecified in the literal record. Nearly equal replacement lengths for every fixed H and epsilon require the actual primary threshold; guessing it would change the task.

Cited successor already states exact Corollary 2.11 and Theorem 3.3. Read Section 3 proof and initial Section 2 machinery, not the entire Section 2 chain. Connectedness/Eulerian convention needs care; disjoint cycles would only expose wording. No new credit.

Exact saturation and all minimizers for every n>=5 is stronger than constructing a sparse saturated family. Pendant attachment at a degree-two vertex matters. No lower-bound or exhaustive equality mechanism.

All sufficiently large edge counts, every fixed wheel size, and equality cases are required. Record already supplies candidate sharp inequalities; an individual join or matching example supplies no new outcome. Body not checked.
All-n balanced Boolean nonlinearity is the full target; an n=8 certificate excluding 118 is only one parameter. Walsh-spectrum feasibility alone does not give the required classification for every n.
Supremum of uniform deterministic polynomial-time attack exponents with all fixed epsilon is a complexity threshold, not an individual lattice attack. No sharp impossibility mechanism.

Worst-case linear share size ranges over all monotone access structures. Counting can give coarse lower bounds but does not identify the optimal exponential exponent; no matching full-scope construction.
All-tree maximum with six piecewise branches, exceptional n=9,21, and extremal classification needs a structural recurrence with equality tracking. Small tree enumeration is not a full route.

Actual source Theorem 6/Corollary 7 settle every finite board, and Theorem 11/Corollary 12 settle both infinite boards. Read all local proofs and definitions. Four-line parity, bounding-box identities and translate elimination are already posted mechanisms.

Universal characterization of zero codegree density needs precise layered-label convention and the meaning of uniform density. No construction or counting transfer proves both directions; source body unreviewed.
Every fixed r>=5 and all sufficiently large n plus an exact ceiling need both saturation construction and lower bound. A finite cycle-free example or the r=5 case would not resolve the family.

Unit-distance upper bound n^(1+epsilon) for every epsilon is the full planar asymptotic problem. No incidence estimate with the needed exponent; supplied GitHub-like audit source is outside permitted routes.

Must hit all maximum independent sets with o(n) vertices uniformly over graphs with linear independence. A random hitting set needs control of the whole set system, not one independent set; no such bound established.

Factor two must hold for every input and every greedy tie-breaking sequence. A favorable tie-break or bounded string search cannot settle it; overlap charging lacks a universal amortization inequality.

Ordinary facet counts admit elementary expressions via minimal/maximal elements, covers and maximal chains, but the record also demands structural/sharp information and marked decomposition variants. Repeating the count formula is a helper, not full resolution.

For each fixed dimension the exponent error must be o(n^d). A hypergraph-container/supersaturation route is plausible but requires quantitative lattice sum-free stability; not a short certificate or established full route.
All prime-power exponent vectors control annihilator equivalence and boxicity. Reducing vertices to divisor vectors is routine preprocessing, not an exact boxicity formula for arbitrary N.
Eventual periodicity for every signature-(1,1) cubic requires exact dynamical definitions and global termination/recurrence. Experiments on selected cubics do not prove the quantified assertion.

Critical ell^(q/2) endpoint in every scaling-admissible triple needs analytic orthonormal restriction estimates. Interpolating noncritical bounds leaves the endpoint unresolved; no bounded algebraic certificate.

Arbitrary finite color families of infinite subgraphs and broader pattern preservation require exact winning conditions and strategy classification. Countable Ramsey alone does not give a Maker strategy under adversarial edge claims.

Decidability uniformly for every pair of coprime bases and every existential formula needs an effective elimination or arithmetic encoding. Testing formulas is irrelevant; cited claimed proof body unreviewed.
All n,k,t tensor-spectral extremizers include competing Frankl families, not just a large-n star regime. Ordinary EKR cardinality alone is insufficient for tensor spectral radius and equality cases.

Largest guaranteed two-way bisection bound for every fixed d and sufficiently large m includes infinitely many equality constructions. Integer rounding and semidegree versus outdegree must be fixed from source; random cuts give only a coarse baseline.
All Segre pushforwards for every family and n demand universal generating coefficients and intersection-theoretic identities. Finite n calculations would be helpers; no short full-series route.

Arbitrary label spaces and two independent dimensions enter the minimax rate. Finite-class concentration does not address DS/Natarajan separation or logarithmic losses; source model definitions needed.

All n and both at-most-one/exactly-one attack variants need extremal upper bounds and uniform constructions. n=1 exposes an exactly-one wording endpoint only, expressly ineligible for credit; no search invested.

Every finite commutative ring plus two graph invariants is a broad classification request. Ring decomposition does not by itself yield exact boxicity or threshold dimension; no closed full-scope route.

Actual source Question 1.2/Theorem 1.3 is the exact tau<=nu_S assertion. Read definitions and full incidence-gadget local proof, Lemmas 3.1-4.2. External bidirected packing-covering lemma is stated, not independently audited. Reproducing this reduction earns no credit.

Optimal alpha-order uniform over all open sets depends on capacity geometry, not a single Hardy test domain. No matching universal estimate and sharpness family derived; claimed alpha^-2 body unreviewed.

Every mapping-class orbit and every length is required, but the claimed exact formulas and word-length convention are absent from the literal record. Cannot promote a single orbit count or inferred formula.

Confinement and projection hypotheses are not specified in the literal statement. Arbitrarily many zero-projection components would only be relevant after checking those hypotheses; no counterexample claimed.

Exact flow sensitivity for arbitrary f needs explicit preprocessing, space and query tradeoffs. A table of all updates or rerunning max-flow is not the intended efficient oracle; no nontrivial compact mechanism.
All number fields and finite S with eventual equality at every large depth requires motivic/arithmetic input. Verifying one field or one depth is not a resolution.
Least B(d) for every d>=5 needs sharp arithmetic threshold, not an improved sufficient Birch bound. No lower-bound family and matching general theorem.

Pairwise moment constraints suggest a finite LP certificate on a chosen n, but arbitrary monotone submodular f and all marginals need a structural extremal reduction or a genuine violating instance. No such instance established; source successor unchecked.

Exact Gabor frame set for all positive a,b needs analytic lower-frame control outside infinitely many rational hyperbolas. Zak-transform finite fibers alone cannot settle irrational densities uniformly.

Every code and fusion pattern with at most one physical success needs the actual fusion/failure model. Stabilizer/parity-check special cases cannot characterize all codes without a general information constraint.

Minimum integral lattice basis and all-weight characterization involve unimodularity and lattice optimization. A fundamental cycle basis gives existence but no minimum-weight optimum or all-graph classification.

Exact finite communication for all d and arbitrary measurements requires full protocol/impossibility model, including allowable shared randomness. Finite samples or approximate simulation do not meet exactness.

Source Definition 1.1 and Theorems 1.2/4.1 already give ternary strings for every length with epsilon=2001/2002. Read main Section 4 proof. Brinkhuis family, local-lemma and appendix constants remain external/unaudited dependencies; no new construction credit.

Literal question is general algorithmic decidability for all nonnegative matrices, much broader than named finite Baker/Ashley instances. A strong-shift-equivalence chain for one pair is insufficient.

All oriented graphs determined by both characteristic polynomials require an exact classification up to isomorphism. Finite cospectral tests or sufficient arithmetic criteria cannot cover the full quantifier.
Uniform positive subconvex saving over the full level family requires automorphic analysis. A numerical central value or fixed representation cannot certify the bound.

Explicit ellipsoid family and oracle promise are only referenced, not defined. Query lower bounds depend on these details and the accuracy convention; generic convex optimization arguments cannot certify this endpoint.
Every finite q>=1 with exact leading constant includes the difficult q=1 endpoint. Dimensional scaling or q=2 calculations do not establish those constants uniformly.

For every k and all N in one congruence class, regular Cayley tournament must be simultaneously vertex-critical for two invariants. A small tournament certificate or one prime order misses the quantified construction.
Every planar induced-minor exclusion and every forbidden induced star needs a bounded tree-independence decomposition theorem. Bounded-degree or one fixed H cases are not a full-scope route.
